nodes.name: Ammonia annealing
nodes.procedure: The fabrication process for Co-Ni₃N nanorods consists of two major steps, i.e., the hydrothermal growth of the source NiCo₂O₄ nanorods array and the ammonia annealing at a proper temperature. The Co-Ni₃N heterostructure array is formed by thermal annealing NiCo₂O₄ precursor nanowires under an optimized condition, during which the nanowire morphology is retained (Detailed synthesis conditions are given in the experimental part in the Supporting Information)
nodes.source_text: The Co-Ni₃N heterostructure array is formed by thermal annealing NiCo₂O₄ precursor nanowires under an optimized condition... the ammonia annealing at a proper temperature

nodes.procedure: Thermal annealing NiO nanorod source material in ammonia, maintaining the morphology of source NiO nanorod (detailed synthesis conditions given in experimental part in Supporting Information)
nodes.source_text: the Ni₃N nanophase maintains the morphology of its source NiO nanorod

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms Co-Ni₃N nanoarrays (diameter ≈80 nm, length ≈1 μm) are composed of tiny nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) studies (Figure 1b and Figure S3d, Supporting Information), the Co - Ni₃N nanoarrays (diameter ≈80 nm, length ≈1 μm) are composed of tiny nanoparticles...

properties.features: Layered structure with dashed lines indicating planes

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows coexistence of Co (100) and Ni₃N (002) lattice fringes with clear epitaxial interface in Co-Ni₃N nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattices of both Ni₃N and Co are visible in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (Figure 1c)... there is clear demonstration for the coexistence of lattice fringes of metallic Co and Ni₃N, which are explicitly discerned in Figure 1d with clear interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mappings confirm distribution of Ni, Co, and N corresponding to Co-Ni₃N nanorod profiles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mappings of Ni, Co, and N correspond well to those profiles of Co - Ni₃N nanorods in Figure 1e.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Co-Ni₃N shows Ni₃N peaks at (110) 38.9°, (111) 44.4°, (113) 78.4° and Co peaks at (102) 62.4°, (110) 75.9°; source NiCo₂O₄ matches JCPDS 73-1702.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further examination of the crystal structure of the Co Ni₃N nanoarrays are made by the X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Figure 2a, the XRD spectrum of the source material corresponds well to the spinel NiCo₂O₄ structure... typical peaks of Ni₃N ((110) at 2θ = 38.9°, (111) at 2θ = 44.4°, (113) at 2θ = 78.4°) and metallic Co ((102) at 2θ = 62.4°, (110) at 2θ = 75.9°) are observed...

properties.description: Crystal plane visualization in atomic structure

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-Ni₃N XPS shows Co 2p at 778.1/794.3 eV (Co⁰), Ni 2p at 853.1/871.0 eV (low valence Ni in Ni₃N), N 1s at 398 eV; Ni 2p binding energy slightly lower and N 1s 0.7 eV lower than Ni₃N alone; Ni:N atomic ratio 2.9:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of XPS spectrum for Co 2p signal (Figure 2b) in Co-Ni₃N nanorods indicates that Co is mainly at zero valence state (located at 778.1 and 794.3 eV)... two sharp peaks at around 853.1 and 871.0 eV (Figure 2c) belong to Ni 2p in Ni₃N... for an identical peak, the binding energy of Ni 2p is slightly lower in Co-Ni₃N than that in Ni₃N... The binding energy of N 1s in Co-Ni₃N... is 398 and 398.7 eV... The atomic concentration ratio of Ni to N is calculated to be 2.9:1...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Ni-N stretching mode peak at ≈460 cm⁻¹ for both Co-Ni₃N and Ni₃N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the Raman shift peaks in Co-Ni₃N and Ni₃N are located in the similar position of ≈460 cm⁻¹ (Figure S6a, Supporting Information), which is in accordance with the stretching mode of Ni-N bond.
